S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a written incident report and known causes or corrective actions within 10 calendar days. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a credible safety risk for their model, providing immediate precautions and a contact for updates.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum allowed failure rate is 5%. Manufacturers shall submit per-model test results and supporting methods to the regulator and provide the complete results to customers of that model automatically, including with purchase information and updates after retesting. Regulators may require interim safeguards or restrict sales where warranted by the risk; exceeding the limit alone does not automatically require a market ban.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New home battery models placed on the market 24 months or more after adoption of this standard must support remote emergency shut-off. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers must enable remote shut-off, where technically feasible, within six years; where it is not feasible, they must notify owners and provide safe-use guidance and any available mitigation.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units placed on the market must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. Existing installed units are not subject to a retrofit requirement under this section, but manufacturers must provide owners with any applicable safe-use guidance.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, based on regulator-reviewed incident and installed-unit data, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers. The regulator must review the evidence and require appropriate corrective action; a mandatory recall is required where the regulator determines that the evidence indicates a serious or imminent risk.

document.section_notes: The final text removes the automatic recall at 8 per 100,000 incidents: crossing that threshold now triggers only prompt notification and open-ended regulator corrective action, with recall reserved for a serious or imminent risk finding. S2 keeps the 5% limit, but exceeding it never requires a sales stop, which protects a model like Northwind's Hearth 10. S3 gives installed units six years for remote shut-off and S4 sets suppression at 36 months, while S1 reporting is strict and fully within the safe range.
